historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (0.8%), rounded; the base path averages ~0.75%/yr over 10 years
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (5.9%/7.0%) diverges by far more than 30% from revenue CAGR (-1.5%/0.8%): book value compounds only because ~US$300-400M/yr of owner FCF is retained after US$150-200M of dividends, not because the business is growing. Equity CAGR is therefore rejected as the growth anchor. EPS 3-yr CAGR of 73% is an artefact of the FY2022 trough (investment impairments cut EPS to US$0.36) and is ignored.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income): FY2020 553.9, FY2021 613.6, FY2022 303.8, FY2023 416.7, FY2024 385.4, FY2025 318.2 (margins 32.8% -> 18.1%). Owner-FCF 5-yr CAGR (-10.5%) is below reported FCF (-7.6%) because interest income more than doubled over the period (US$86M -> US$117M) while operating cash generation fell; a rising share of reported FCF is now yield on the cash pile rather than platform cash flow. SBC, by contrast, has collapsed (6.1% of revenue in FY2022 to 2.4% in FY2025 and ~0.8% in H1 2026), which flatters the 3-yr owner-FCF CAGR (+1.6%).

scenario_narratives.base: Weibo is a mature, ex-growth public-square platform. Advertising (84% of revenue) is roughly flat in USD terms: Alibaba (+49% in FY2025) and resilient verticals (auto/NEV, local services, internet services) offset a shrinking ex-Alibaba advertiser base, VAS grows modestly, and reported revenue drifts from -1% to +2% a year through FY2035. The FY2026 step-down in operating margin (H1 26% vs 30%) from higher content, production and marketing spend to defend engagement is treated as permanent, with AI-driven eCPM gains preventing further erosion rather than restoring the old 35%+ adjusted EBITDA margin. Cash taxes ramp to 25% as dividend-repatriation withholding grows. The value is mostly balance sheet: net cash of US$0.76B plus haircut long-term investments and the SINA receivable are worth ~US$5.1/share before any operating cash flow is counted.
scenario_narratives.bull: The 2025-26 ad softness is cyclical, not structural. Chinese consumption recovers, the auto/NEV launch cycle and celebrity/entertainment marketing keep growing, Alibaba's shopping-festival spend continues to compound, VAS sustains double-digit growth and AI ad tools raise yield per impression, giving 3-4% revenue growth for five years. Defensive marketing spend normalises and adjusted EBITDA margin recovers to ~32% by FY2031. The US$200M buyback is executed at depressed prices (value-neutral in the model, but it funds the flat count) and the HK listing plus continued dividends keep the China discount from widening.
scenario_narratives.bear: Weibo's displacement from brand-marketing budgets is structural: Douyin, Xiaohongshu and WeChat Channels own discovery and conversion, the advertiser count keeps shrinking (0.6M -> 0.4M in one year), MAU attrition continues, and a further CAC crackdown on celebrity-gossip content removes the engagement engine. Alibaba, now ~12% of ad revenue, redirects budget. Revenue falls ~25% by FY2033 and margin settles at 20%. The VIE/HFCAA tail (forced restructuring, US delisting with the HK line as the only venue) and further impairments of the RMB investment portfolio are the reasons this scenario carries a 35% weight rather than the house default 15%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Weibo is valued as a mature, cash-generative advertising platform on fully SBC-expensed owner FCF, with the interest and investment income stripped from the flows and the assets that produce them (net cash, long-term investments at a 50% haircut, the SINA receivable at 75%) added back in the bridge, minority interests deducted once, and the 2030 convertible treated as debt rather than as shares. The China-ADR/VIE premium is charged once, in an 11.5% USD cost of equity used across all scenarios; Weibo-specific operating risk is charged in the scenario paths and a 35% bear weight. Terminal values are capped at 12x (10x bear) owner FCF to avoid assuming a re-rating the stock has never had. The gap between the resulting value and the US$6.33 price is the market's China/VIE/structural-decline discount made explicit; the model does not pretend to know whether that discount closes, which is why the 15% hurdle entry price and the bear case are reported alongside the weighted value.
key_risks_to_valuation: VIE and HFCAA structure: ADS holders hold a contractual claim, not equity in the PRC operating business; an adverse PRC ruling or US delisting is a tail the DCF cannot price except through the bear weight and the country premium.

Balance-sheet value may not reach ADS holders: ~US$5/share of the value is net cash, RMB investments and a loan to the private parent; it depends on continued repatriation (10% withholding), the SINA receivable being collected, and the investment portfolio not being impaired further (H1 2026 already shows ~US$90M of non-operating losses).
Structural ad-share loss: advertiser count fell from 0.6M to 0.4M in one year; if ex-Alibaba revenue keeps falling 4%+ a year the bear path is the base path.
Alibaba concentration (~12% of ad revenue and rising) plus Alibaba's shareholder position: a budget reallocation would remove the one growing ad stream.
Margin compression continuing beyond FY2026 (content/production costs, CAC compliance burden) -- each 1pp of permanent EBITDA margin is roughly US$0.5-0.6/share.
RMB depreciation: USD-reported revenue was -4% constant-currency in Q2 2026 vs +2% reported; the growth path is in USD and inherits FX.

Long-term-investment haircut judgment: 50% is a round-number view of an undisclosed mix; each 10pp is ~US$0.65/share. 'Other non-current assets' (US$1.25B) are excluded entirely, which may be too harsh.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API, NASDAQ regular close at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 6.27-12.77. Parity-checked against 9898.HK at USDHKD 7.8463 (both Yahoo, 2026-10-02).

data_sources.qualitative: research/WB/Reports/WB_Analysis.json (2026-10-04): business model, Alibaba concentration, CAC enforcement history, VIE/HFCAA risk, Q1/Q2 2026 commentary, dividend and buyback programmes.

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 20-F cash flow statement add-back (us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation, US$42.067M). Weibo publishes no combined 'SBC incl. equity-award taxes' figure and no separate net-share-settlement tax line in financing activities, so the add-back is used alone. H1 2026 SBC was only US$6.6M (6-K non-GAAP reconciliation), i.e. ~0.8% of revenue.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and quote are both USD, so no conversion is applied. The underlying economics are RMB (essentially 100% PRC revenue); Q2 2026 revenue was +2% reported but -4% constant-currency, so the USD growth path carries RMB translation noise. Parity check on the 1:1 Hong Kong secondary listing: 9898.HK HK$49.68 (2026-10-02 close) / USDHKD 7.8463 = US$6.33, exactly the NASDAQ close, confirming the ADS:share ratio of 1:1 and the quote basis.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-02T20:00:00Z regular close (Friday); not an after-hours print
inputs.share_count_basis: 246.0M = Q2 2026 basic weighted shares 239.46M (6-K) + ~6.6M dilutive options/RSUs. The 6-K diluted count of 271.55M also includes ~25M if-converted shares from the US$330M 2030 convertible notes (conversion price ~US$13 vs a US$6.33 price); those notes are carried as DEBT at principal in total_debt, so they are NOT also added to the share count (charging a convert both ways is the share-count double-count). Cross-check: 245.55M ordinary shares issued at 2025-12-31 (us-gaap:CommonStockSharesOutstanding), which already contains the award-reserve shares, agrees within 0.2%. Count held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; buyback_cash is 0 for FY2025 and H1 2026 (no PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock since the US$57.7M in FY2022; basic shares rose 238.6M -> 239.5M YoY), so the flat count is a modelling convention the US$200M Dec-2025 authorisation has not yet funded.
inputs.net_debt_note: Balance sheet at 2026-06-30 (Q2 2026 6-K): cash US$1,639.1M + short-term investments US$997.4M = US$2,636.6M (restricted cash US$2.4M excluded). Debt at PRINCIPAL: US$330M 1.375% convertible senior notes due 2030 (carrying 325.5) + US$750M unsecured senior notes (carrying 746.1) + US$800M long-term bank loans (carrying 795.8) = US$1,880M; there are no short-term borrowings. The CSV TotalDebt of US$2,096.2M is the XBRL LongTermDebt contractual-maturity schedule, which includes future coupon payments (US$69.6M in the next 12 months is one year's interest on the three instruments), so it overstates debt by ~US$216M; flagged for a `make fix`. Net debt = 1,880.0 - 2,636.6 = -756.6 (net cash). Operating lease liabilities (US$42.4M) are excluded: US GAAP operating-lease cost sits inside opex/EBITDA, i.e. lease treatment (B), charged once in the flows.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Flows are USD-reported, so the rate is USD-built: 10-yr UST ~4.1% + beta 1.1 x ERP 5.0% = 9.6%, plus a 2.0pp China country / VIE-structure premium (sovereign CDS spread plus the untested contractual-control claim and HFCAA overhang that apply to every PRC ADR, not to Weibo specifically) = ~11.6% cost of equity, rounded to 11.5%. No leverage credit is taken: the US$1.88B of bonds and loans is more than covered by US$2.64B of cash and short-term investments, so the firm is economically unlevered and WACC = cost of equity. Market-value weights would push WACC toward 6% only because the equity is depressed, which would be circular. Risk is charged ONCE: the discount rate carries the generic China-ADR/VIE premium; Weibo-specific operating risk (ad-share loss to Douyin/Xiaohongshu, CAC enforcement, Alibaba concentration, margin compression) lives in the scenario paths and the elevated bear weight. The same WACC is used in all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost: US GAAP operating-lease expense (US$13.0M cash paid FY2025) is already inside cost of revenue/opex and therefore inside the EBITDA margin path; lease liabilities (US$42.4M) are excluded from net debt. No lease_cost_pct_path is needed because the margin is anchored to post-lease-expense GAAP operating income.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are modelled on a consolidated basis (EBITDA margin anchored to consolidated operating income), so the non-controlling interests are deducted ONCE in the equity bridge at book: US$56.5M NCI + US$17.8M redeemable NCI at 2026-06-30 = -US$74.3M. NCI's share of net income is small (US$3.0M FY2025, US$0.8M H1 2026), so book is a fair proxy.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, consumer internet', plus the non-US adaptations file for currency, excluded income/matching assets, NCI and charge-risk-once). Weibo is an advertising-funded social platform with ~84% ad / ~16% VAS revenue; it is not a bank, REIT, holdco or distressed name, so no other route applies. No prior DCF exists (fresh build; no memory entry). OWNER FCF: last_fcf = reported FCF 477.111 - SBC 42.067 - interest income 116.826 = 318.218 (18.1% of revenue). Interest income is stripped because the gross cash pile (US$2.64B) that earns it is added back in the bridge; note FY2025 reported OCF is after US$75.3M of interest PAID on the bonds/loans (US GAAP), so the FY0 unlevered equivalent is ~US$378M (21.5%) -- the forward component build is unlevered and subtracts net debt, so the two are consistent; the year-1 component FCF (~US$330M, 18.4%) sits below that because the FY2026 margin compression (H1 2026 operating margin 26.3% vs 30.4%, Q2 28% non-GAAP vs 36%) is built in. EXCLUDED-INCOME / MATCHING-ASSET RULE: FY2025 pre-tax income of 605.6 vs operating income of 464.8 implies ~US$106M of interest, dividend and investment gains outside the operating flows; all of it is excluded from the forward build, so its source assets are brought into the bridge: long-term investments (US$1,602.8M at 2026-06-30: measurement-alternative private-company stakes US$292M at Dec-25, equity-method and available-for-sale preferred positions, all RMB-denominated and illiquid, with a record of impairments -- FY2022 pre-tax income fell to 128 on ~350 of investment losses, and H1 2026 pre-tax 142 vs operating 230 implies another ~US$90M of non-operating losses) taken at a 50% HAIRCUT (US$801.4M); and the US$440.3M 'Amount due from SINA' (interest-bearing loan to the private controlling shareholder) at 75% (US$330.2M) for related-party recoverability risk. Each 10pp on the long-term-investment haircut is ~US$0.65/share. 'Other non-current assets' of US$1,245.5M (long-term deposits/wealth-management products, deferred tax, long-term prepayments, ROU assets -- composition not disclosed in the 6-K) is NOT added: a deliberate conservative omission, since part of the stripped interest income probably comes from it. CONVERTIBLE: US$330M 2030 notes treated as debt (conversion price ~US$13 vs price US$6.33) and excluded from the share count; see share_count_basis. HORIZON: 10 years, because the base/bull margin paths are still moving in year 5 and the bear path only bottoms in year 5. TERMINAL CAP 12x (10x bear) per the method's 'structurally slower business' guidance -- Weibo has traded at 3-6x EV/EBITDA for five years and a 20x cap would be a re-rating bet. FY2026 GUIDANCE: none numeric (company does not guide); H1 2026 revenue US$875.2M (+4.0%), Q3 ad revenue flagged to face 'certain pressure' from high comparatives, so FY2026 base growth is +2%.

bear.rationale: Structural: the SME advertiser base keeps leaving for Douyin/Xiaohongshu/WeChat Channels, MAU attrition continues, a further CAC enforcement round curbs the celebrity-gossip content that drives engagement, and Alibaba redirects budget. Revenue falls ~25% to ~US$1.31B by FY2033 and adjusted EBITDA margin settles at 20% because content and compliance costs cannot be cut as fast as revenue. Terminal growth 1%, cap 10x. Same WACC as base/bull (risk is in the flows and the weight, not stacked in the rate).

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +2%: H1 2026 +4.0% reported (about flat constant-currency), Q3 ad revenue guided to 'certain pressure'. FY2027-28 -1%/yr as ex-Alibaba advertiser attrition (count 0.6M -> 0.4M, ex-Alibaba ad revenue -4% in FY2025) continues to outrun Alibaba and VAS growth; then stabilisation at 0-2% nominal as the platform settles into its entertainment/news/PR niche. Revenue in FY2035 ~US$1.89B, 8% above FY2025.
base.margin_rationale: Adjusted (pre-SBC) EBITDA margin was 35-37% in FY2021-24 and 32.2% in FY2025; H1 2026 ~30% vs ~37% a year earlier and H2 2025 ~28%, so FY2026 lands near 27.5%. Held at 27% thereafter: the content/marketing spend needed to defend engagement is treated as permanent, with AI eCPM gains only offsetting further erosion.
base.sbc_rationale: FY2025 2.4%, H1 2026 0.8%. Anchored at 1.2% for FY2026 and normalised to 1.5% (some re-grant for retention after the collapse in award values); historical 4-6% is not re-assumed.
base.capex_da_rationale: D&A 3.3% (FY2025 3.36%); capex 2.8% (FY2024 3.5%, FY2025 2.4%, H1 2026 well under 1%). The gap is the amortisation of acquired intangibles, which is not replaced.
base.tax_rationale: Cash taxes FY2025 US$94.4M = 20% of EBIT; GAAP ETR 24% FY2025 and 27% H1 2026. PRC statutory 25% with HNTE 15% at some subsidiaries, plus 5-10% withholding on dividends repatriated to fund the ADS dividend. Ramp 22% -> 25%.
base.wc_rationale: Ad-supported; deferred revenue flat at US$70-100M, receivables ~23% of revenue. With revenue roughly flat the working-capital change rounds to zero.

bull.rationale: Ad softness proves cyclical: Chinese consumption recovers, auto/NEV, local services and celebrity-marketing verticals keep growing, Alibaba spend keeps compounding, VAS sustains double-digit growth (+19% Q2 2026) and AI eCPM gains lift yield per user without MAU growth. Margin returns to the FY2021-24 range of ~32% adjusted EBITDA by FY2031 as defensive marketing spend normalises.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 35% because Weibo meets three of the method's named triggers: a single-regulator dependency (CAC has acted against Weibo in 2021 and September 2025 and its content rules bite directly on the engagement model), a growing single-customer concentration (Alibaba ~US$174M and +49% while everyone else shrank), and a VIE/HFCAA structural tail that the flows cannot express. Bull held to 20% because it needs two independent things to go right -- a Chinese consumption recovery AND a margin recovery to the FY2021-24 range -- and the advertiser-count data points the other way. Base 45%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
